stem: An idealised trolley moves horizontally while a constant force acts vertically. What is the work done by this force on the trolley during the horizontal displacement?

options.text: Not enough information about the speed

conditions: The stated force is purely vertical and constant.

scaffolds.text: Represent the direction of displacement and the force as two arrows.
Relate the angle between force and displacement to work.
Determine the component of the force along the displacement before multiplying by the distance.

answer.summary: C — Zero work by the vertical force.
reasoning: Work of a constant force is the scalar product of the force and displacement.
The perpendicular vertical force has no component along the horizontal displacement.
Therefore its work is zero, regardless of the trolley's speed.
answer.check: Doubling horizontal distance still gives no work from a purely perpendicular force.
